anomalies.observed: R8 (10k) pulls the gate net of T5 (IRLR2905, the low-side switch for the H8 +24V load) up to +3V3. The gate is also driven by IO10 through R26 (100 Ω) and by the collector of T6. With no active drive, the gate sits high and T5 conducts. By contrast, the equivalent ATO switch T3 has its gate pulled to GND through R31 (10k).
anomalies.expected: A switch that drives a 24 V pump or valve should default to OFF during reset and boot, when the ESP32 GPIO is high-impedance. That requires the gate pull resistor to go to GND, as on the T3 stage, not to +3V3.
anomalies.impact: If IO10 is high-impedance at reset, the pump output may energise at power-up or reset until firmware drives the gate low, which is an unintended dosing or actuation hazard.

anomalies.observed: The float-high input line NET0060 (the pull-down R46 to GND, and the IO1 path) is decoupled by C68 to +3V3. The float-low line NET0035 is decoupled by C45 to GND. The two input filters are inconsistent.
anomalies.expected: A 100 nF filter capacitor on an input that is pulled down to GND would normally go to GND, matching C45 on the other float input.
anomalies.impact: Minor. The filter is less effective, and the float-switch input behaves differently from its counterpart. There is no DC effect.
